h: Trusting the Prayer Whose Answer Remains Hidden

p: "And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me,
and my Lord has forgotten me."
the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer.
hearkening to the voice of His servant?"
And from this the Gemara (Berachos 6b) expounds:
"What is 'hearkening to the voice of His servant'?
If you say to a prophet
or another man to do with prayer,
that because one prays his prayer
he hearkens to the voice of a prophet
with which HaKadosh Baruch Hu calls him
that he is His servant," etc.
is in the aspect of a servant,
and I am like a minister before the king."
That is, Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai
and is like a minister before the king;
which is like a servant before the king,
"like the eyes of servants to their masters."
And this is the meaning of
which is the power of prayer,
"hearkening to the voice of His servant":
that Hashem Yisbarach calls him His servant,
for he is in the aspect of a servant.
And from where does he hear this?
Only according to what is said
in the name of our master Rebbe Elimelech,
on what the Mishnah says (ibid., Berachos 5:5):
"If my prayer is fluent in my mouth,
I know that he is accepted":
sends the prayer into his mouth,
that he still walks in darkness,
that he has not yet been saved,
and he does not yet see
and this is "and has no light,"
from the benefit of the prayer.
"Let him trust in the Name of Hashem
that He is mighty and all-capable
and the Master of all the powers,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (טוּר וְשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן ה)
as written (Tur and Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 5);
that is, on this he should rely,
is only from the power of Hashem,
Who looks ahead to the good;
and let him not despair of mercy,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם נא, א)
And about this it says afterward (ibid. 51:1):
"Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness,
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רמ, א)
and it is found in the holy Zohar (III 240a):
and it is found in the holy Zohar:
and this corresponds to the Name Adnus,
And this answers what Tziyon said,
to this He said, "who pursue righteousness."
answers what she said, "Hashem has forsaken me."
That is, the main thing is
then you have no reason to despair.
and many ages have already passed,
and we have not yet been saved,
רַק הַבִּיטוּ אֶל צוּר חוּצַּבְתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר
but "look to the rock from which you were hewn," etc.,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר (יְבָמוֹת סד, א)
along the lines of what it says (Yevamos 64a):
and they had no hope at all
מִכָּל מָקוֹם פָּקַד אוֹתָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
So too you should trust and rely
"Joy and gladness will be found in her":
this corresponds to Torah and prayer
for both of them will come
"When You did awesome things that we did not hope for."
